When a new memory is stored: (1) find semantic neighbors via HNSW vector search, (2) run LLM analysis via llm_gateway to extract connections/tags/context updates, (3) update neighbor Memory nodes via Cypher. The evolution engine (evolution.py) is already backend-agnostic — it just needs a store that supports neighbor lookup and metadata updates. old_value: {"id":"python-factory-d77","title":"Graph-RAG: KG construction pipeline in KB brick Neo4j adapter","description":"Article reference: 'Stop AI Agent Hallucinations' by Elizabeth Fuentes (the-article.md). Technique 1: Graph-RAG. WHAT: Add automatic entity/relationship extraction during kb_ingest when Neo4j is the backend. Currently KB's Neo4j adapter (components/kb/src/factory/kb/runtime/retrieval/neo4j_vector.py) stores flat KBDocument nodes with embeddings. Need to extract entities and relationships from ingested text and write them as proper graph nodes/edges. WHY: Enables Text2Cypher pattern — LLM writes Cypher queries for aggregation/counting/relationship questions instead of guessing from vector chunks. Paper shows RAG fabricates statistics while Graph-RAG computes exact answers. IMPLEMENTATION: (1) Add neo4j-graphrag as optional pip dep of KB brick's neo4j adapter. (2) Add extract_entities option to Neo4jVectorStore.add() — when True, run LLM-driven entity/relationship extraction via neo4j-graphrag after storing the document. Extracted entities go into Neo4j as proper graph nodes with relationships. (3) Add routing guidance to chat agent system prompt: for aggregation/counting/relationship queries, prefer graph_query with Cypher over kb_search. (4) Default extract_entities=True when backend is neo4j. FILES: components/kb/src/factory/kb/runtime/retrieval/neo4j_vector.py (add extraction), components/kb/BRICK.yaml (add neo4j-graphrag dep), components/agent/src/factory/agent/runtime/companion/ (routing guidance). REFERENCE: cognee memory adapter already does entity extraction — similar pattern.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"feature","owner":"wdaniero@amazon.com","created_at":"2026-03-10T15:29:13Z","created_by":"Daniel Rodrigo","updated_at":"2026-03-10T15:29:13Z"}

WHAT: Replace the static ALLOWED_BRICK_PREFIXES filter in components/agent/src/factory/agent/runtime/companion/tools.py with per-query semantic filtering using Neo4j HNSW vector indexes. Currently every query gets the same ~50 tools regardless of intent. Paper shows 86.4% error reduction and 89% token savings with semantic filtering. WHY: With 300+ MCP tools, the chat agent wastes tokens and makes more selection errors. A security question should get security tools, an ML question should get ML tools. IMPLEMENTATION: (1) At agent startup or tool registry change, create ToolDescription nodes in Neo4j with name, description, brick prefix. Embed descriptions via existing embedder. (3) Fallback: if Neo4j unavailable, fall back to current static prefix filtering. (4) Use existing graph brick infrastructure — graph_create_vector_index, graph_set_embedding, graph_vector_search — no FAISS dependency needed. FILES: components/agent/src/factory/agent/runtime/companion/tools.py (main change), components/agent/src/factory/agent/runtime/chat.py (pass query to select_tools), components/agent/src/factory/agent/mcp/tools.py (_build_chat_tools passes query). BENEFITS FOR KIRO: When Kiro talks through Companion-X via agent_reason, the chat agent gets semantically filtered tools. Root cause: ResizeObserver useEffect in graph-view.tsx had [selected] in its dependency array. On node click, setSelected fires → effect tears down and re-creates the observer → measure() calls setDims() → new width/height props passed to ForceGraph2D → canvas re-renders, disrupting the click event cycle. Fix: removed selected from the dependency array (eslint-disable comment added). The ResizeObserver only needs to observe the container element, not react to selection changes.

Removed the auto-expand block from loadTopology in use-graph-data.ts. The batchRun loop was calling graph_get_neighbors for the first 40 nodes in batches of 5 = 8 sequential async rounds on every load. Now loadTopology only calls graph_find_entities and sets nodes with an empty links array. Edges load lazily via expandNode when a user clicks a node. {"description":"Timeline SSE only shows API-proxied tool calls. Root cause: instrumentation._emit() calls in-process event_bus which is isolated per process. Kiro calls MCP server directly (port 8000) — its events never reach the API server's SSE endpoint. Fix: instrumentation._emit() should also call events_publish via MCP aggregator (same pattern as blockchain/games/ML bricks). SSE endpoint subscribes to events brick instead of in-process bus. This fails on real-world scenarios where: (1) CWE hierarchies matter (CWE-639 is a child of CWE-863 but scores as a miss), (2) findings point to different layers of the same bug (VetsController.java vs VetClinicsPageController.java), (3) semantic similarity matters more than string equality. Proposal: pair the deterministic gt_score with Strands LLM evaluators (faithfulness, response_relevance, output) to produce a hybrid score. The deterministic pass gives P/R/F1 on exact matches; the LLM eval pass scores semantic closeness for near-misses. Together they answer: did the tool find what's in the GT DB, and how close did it get? Discovered during PenPal vs Shepherd GT comparison where Finding #1 (VetsController IDOR) was clearly the same bug family as the GT (VetClinicsPageController IDOR, CWE-639) but scored 0/0/0 on all deterministic modes.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"feature","owner":"wdaniero@amazon.com","created_at":"2026-03-31T18:39:30Z","created_by":"Daniel Rodrigo","updated_at":"2026-03-31T18:39:30Z"}

{"description":"Every page takes ~3s because each makes 2-5 MCP round-trips through browser\u003eNext.js\u003eCognito\u003eAgentCore Gateway\u003eRuntime\u003eDynamoDB. Even cached, each hop is ~500-800ms. Key problems: (1) DUPLICATE FETCHES - Dashboard fetches findings 2x (SummaryPills + RecentPanel both call finding list). (2) WATERFALL - App detail fetches app first, THEN fires 3 more calls sequentially. (3) NO CLIENT CACHE - navigating between pages re-fetches everything. (4) OVER-FETCHING - registry requests 10K apps every load. (5) NO TIMEOUT - slow gateway just hangs. Solutions: SWR/TanStack Query for cross-page caching, dedup identical calls, parallelize waterfalls, AbortController with 5s timeout, server-side cache in /api/mcp (60s TTL), MCP-side pagination. NOT mock-swap (causes inconsistent numbers mid-page)."}

{"description":"## Symptom

Companion-X chat sidebar no longer renders the Thinking panel
(`<CopilotChatReasoningMessage>`) on assistant turns. User reports
"we used to show thought as a call inside chat but that's no longer
displayed". Confirmed via Playwright probe of the running API process
and SSE-stream inspection on `/ag-ui/run`: zero `REASONING_MESSAGE_*`
events emitted across a chat run.

## Root cause

Two-edged config gap, not a code bug:

1. `COMPANION_X_CHAT_MODEL` is empty in the running API process env
   (verified via `ps eww`). Falls through to `_resolve_chat_model()`
   returning `None`, then `build_chat_model(None)` -> `_resolve_model(None)`
   picks a Strands default. The default may resolve to a thinking-capable
   model (chat says "I am Claude") but the model_id passed into
   `_supports_thinking()` is None, so the predicate fails.

2. `COMPANION_X_CHAT_THINKING_BUDGET` is unset. `_thinking_budget()`
   returns 0. With budget=0, `additionalModelRequestFields.thinking`
   is never attached to the BedrockModel - Sonnet does not emit
   `reasoning_text` events, AG-UI mapper has nothing to translate
   into `REASONING_MESSAGE_START/CONTENT/END`, CopilotKit's Thinking
   panel has nothing to render.

Strands and FE pipeline are both fine. Canary tests pass:
- components/agent/test/factory/agent/test_strands_mcp_chat_thinking.py
  pins BedrockModel `_get_additional_request_fields` shape.
- bases/api/test/factory/api/test_ag_ui_chat_reasoning.py pins the
  AG-UI trio when `reasoning_text` events arrive.

## Fix (env-only path, ships immediately)

Set in projects/companion_x/.env:

  COMPANION_X_CHAT_MODEL=us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
  COMPANION_X_CHAT_THINKING_BUDGET=16000

Restart the API. SSE stream now emits the trio; Thinking panel renders.

## Bigger fix (UX-correct path) — file as discovered-from sub-issue

User feedback: "that env variable should ALWAYS be on" and "I always
assume all models think". Three follow-ups make the experience match
the mental model:

1. Flip `_thinking_budget()` default from 0 to a sane budget (e.g. 8192)
   when env unset. Treat empty/"0" as explicit-off only. Cost note:
   Bedrock bills thinking output separately at the per-token rate, so
   default-on is a real cost decision — needs strands-expert consult on
   the budget number before flipping.

2. Default `COMPANION_X_CHAT_MODEL` to a thinking-capable model
   (Sonnet 4.6) in .env.example and the local-dev README so a fresh
   clone gets thinking out of the box.

3. Optional: small UI hint in chat header when active model is not
   thinking-capable so user understands why the panel is silent.
   (Haiku/Nova/Llama/GLM5/GPT-OSS cannot natively emit reasoning.)

## Repro

1. Start API with `COMPANION_X_CHAT_MODEL=` (empty) and
   `COMPANION_X_CHAT_THINKING_BUDGET` unset.
2. Open dashboard, send any chat message.
3. Inspect DevTools Network -> POST /ag-ui/run SSE stream. Filter
   for "REASONING_MESSAGE_". Result: zero matches.
4. <CopilotChatReasoningMessage> slot never mounts. Thinking panel
   never appears.

## Acceptance

- Env vars set; SSE stream contains REASONING_MESSAGE_START +
  >=1 REASONING_MESSAGE_CONTENT + REASONING_MESSAGE_END per chat turn.
- Thinking panel renders inline above the assistant message.
- Both pinned tests still pass:
    pytest components/agent/test/factory/agent/test_strands_mcp_chat_thinking.py
    pytest bases/api/test/factory/api/test_ag_ui_chat_reasoning.py

## Files involved (read-only context)

- projects/companion_x/.env (config gap)
- projects/companion_x/.env.example (default-on fix candidate)
- components/agent/src/factory/agent/runtime/adapters/strands_mcp_chat_thinking.py
  (_thinking_budget, _supports_thinking, build_chat_model)
- components/ui/src/factory/ui/runtime/ag_ui_mapper_chat.py
  (_on_reasoning_text, _close_reasoning_if_open)
- frontends/next-dashboard/lib/copilotkit/reasoning-slot.tsx
- frontends/next-dashboard/components/chat/copilot-sidebar.tsx
  (messageView.reasoningMessage slot)

## Tenet

dev-principles.md — Companion-X local dev should "just work" without
env-var-fu. SDK-First: Strands provides the primitive, our defaults
should make it visible by default in dev."}

{"id":"python-factory-f4gjq","title":"lo1g9.4 CSP script-src blocks Next App Router RSC inline scripts; chat unusable","description":"phx2m R2 E2E canary BLOCK. PR #609 (commit 2f7bc7b0) shipped `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` with no nonce/hash strategy. The unit test in `lib/security/__tests__/csp.test.ts` even asserts `'unsafe-inline'` is forbidden. But Next.js App Router emits ~13 inline scripts on every page load — `__next_f.push([1,'7:I[...']` RSC streaming chunks plus dev-mode React Refresh runtime — and these have no nonce and no precomputed hash in the directive. Result: every inline script is blocked, React fibers never attach (`__reactContainer$`/`__reactFiber$` keys absent on body children and on the send button), CopilotKit can't bind to its provider, the status bar reports "Disconnected", and the send-message button stays `disabled` even when the textarea has text. The chat surface is functionally dead.

EVIDENCE (collected via playwright power against http://localhost:3000):

1) HEADERS PRESENT — `fetch('/', {method:'HEAD'})` returns CSP + X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN + COOP same-origin + COEP credentialless + Permissions-Policy + Referrer-Policy. Header wiring works; the directive shape is the problem.

2) CSP RUNTIME ERRORS — console:
   - 13 "Executing inline script violates the following Content Security Policy directive 'script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval''" blocks (one per inline script with sha256 hash).
   - "Evaluating a string as JavaScript violates the following Content Security Policy directive because 'unsafe-eval' is not an allowed source of script" from @next/react-refresh-utils/dist/runtime.js (dev-mode HMR).
   - "Connecting to 'http://localhost:8000/health' violates the following Content Security Policy directive: 'connect-src 'self' https: wss:'" — useHealth poll to the absolute API_URL fails. Today /api/health works through the proxy route, but http://localhost:8000 is a valid configured API_URL.

3) REACT NOT HYDRATED — `Object.keys(document.body.firstChild)` shows zero React fiber/container keys. `document.querySelector('[data-testid=copilot-send-button]')` exists in the SSR HTML but is not React-bound, `btn.disabled === true`, `btn.click()` is a no-op.

4) STATUS BAR DISCONNECTED — useHealth never fires because React doesn't hydrate.

5) CHAT FLOW IMPOSSIBLE — Tried filling the textarea, Enter, button click, native HTMLTextAreaElement.value setter + synthetic input event. Send button stays disabled. Zero `[data-message-role]` messages ever attach.

ROOT CAUSE: lib/security/csp.ts directives are mutually exclusive with Next.js App Router runtime. `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` does not cover Next inline RSC scripts or React Refresh `new Function`.

NEXT.JS COMPATIBLE FIX:
- App Router needs middleware-injected `script-src 'nonce-<random>' 'strict-dynamic'` with the nonce mirrored to <script nonce={nonce}> server-side via `headers()`/`cookies()`. See nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/configuring/content-security-policy.
- Alternatively guard `buildSecurityHeaders()` so dev mode (`process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'`) appends `'unsafe-eval' 'unsafe-inline'` for script-src; production swaps to nonce. Either way the test in csp.test.ts that forbids 'unsafe-inline' must be split into prod/dev variants.

REPRO:
1. `cd frontends/next-dashboard && npm run dev`
2. Open http://localhost:3000
3. DevTools console: ~13 CSP inline-script blocks + eval block
4. Status bar shows "Disconnected", send button disabled even with textarea text

OUT OF SCOPE: McpUiFrame / origin allowlist / validator React components themselves are not reachable for verification because React never hydrates.

Evidence screenshots:
- .agents/.issues/phx2m-r2-csp-breaks-react-refresh-2026-05-29T22-29-00-233Z.png
- .agents/.issues/phx2m-r2-A-blocked-disconnected-2026-05-29T22-30-03-327Z.png

   (verified via `ps eww`). Falls through to `_resolve_chat_model()`
   returning `None`, then `build_chat_model(None)` -> `_resolve_model(None)`
   picks a Strands default. The default may resolve to a thinking-capable
   model (chat says "I am Claude") but the model_id passed into
   `_supports_thinking()` is None, so the predicate fails.

2. `COMPANION_X_CHAT_THINKING_BUDGET` is unset. `_thinking_budget()`
   returns 0. With budget=0, `additionalModelRequestFields.thinking`
   is never attached to the BedrockModel - Sonnet does not emit
   `reasoning_text` events, AG-UI mapper has nothing to translate
   into `REASONING_MESSAGE_START/CONTENT/END`, CopilotKit's Thinking
   panel has nothing to render.

Strands and FE pipeline are both fine. Canary tests pass:
- components/agent/test/factory/agent/test_strands_mcp_chat_thinking.py
  pins BedrockModel `_get_additional_request_fields` shape.
- bases/api/test/factory/api/test_ag_ui_chat_reasoning.py pins the
  AG-UI trio when `reasoning_text` events arrive.

## Fix (env-only path, ships immediately)

Set in projects/companion_x/.env:

  COMPANION_X_CHAT_MODEL=us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
  COMPANION_X_CHAT_THINKING_BUDGET=16000

Restart the API. SSE stream now emits the trio; Thinking panel renders.

## Bigger fix (UX-correct path) — file as discovered-from sub-issue

User feedback: "that env variable should ALWAYS be on" and "I always
assume all models think". Three follow-ups make the experience match
the mental model:

1. Flip `_thinking_budget()` default from 0 to a sane budget (e.g. 8192)
   when env unset. Treat empty/"0" as explicit-off only. Cost note:
   Bedrock bills thinking output separately at the per-token rate, so
   default-on is a real cost decision — needs strands-expert consult on
   the budget number before flipping.

2. Default `COMPANION_X_CHAT_MODEL` to a thinking-capable model
   (Sonnet 4.6) in .env.example and the local-dev README so a fresh
   clone gets thinking out of the box.

3. Optional: small UI hint in chat header when active model is not
   thinking-capable so user understands why the panel is silent.
   (Haiku/Nova/Llama/GLM5/GPT-OSS cannot natively emit reasoning.)

new_value: {"description":"ROOT CAUSE: DiskRegistryStore.save_persona writes \u003cid\u003e.yaml (registry_store.py line 67-71). On a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS APFS default, Windows NTFS) two persona ids differing ONLY by case (e.g. MyAgent vs myagent, or unicode U+0162 vs U+0163) map to the SAME file, so the second save silently OVERWRITES the first. InMemoryRegistryStore keys an exact dict (registry_store.py line 96-99) and keeps BOTH. The two RegistryStore adapters are therefore NOT behaviorally equivalent on case-only-differing ids. IMPACT: low-moderate. _ID_RE (authoring/validation.py line 16) accepts mixed case, so a user CAN author MyAgent then myagent; on macOS/Windows the first persona vanishes silently on reload. Built-ins are unaffected (all lowercase, merge collision is exact/case-sensitive and correct). REPRO deterministic on macOS: DiskRegistryStore save MyAgent then save myagent, load_personas returns only [myagent], MyAgent LOST. ALSO BREAKS the implementer Phase 0 test test_unified_registry_properties.py::test_disk_and_memory_stores_agree (line 105) because its _id_strategy (line 28-33) uses whitelist_categories L,N including cased unicode. SUGGESTED FIX (meta-architect call, touches RegistryStore Protocol case-equivalence semantics): (a) case-safe disk stem, or (b) reject case-collision on save / in _ID_RE, or (c) constrain that test strategy to a case-stable alphabet AND document the disk case-fold caveat in adapter docstring + ports.py. old_value: {"id":"python-factory-iqm3h","title":"MCP endpoint lacks CORS headers — browser IDE (:3456) can't discover tools cross-origin; all Theia panels show 'tool not available'","description":"The Companion-X backend mounts the FastMCP Streamable-HTTP app at /mcp/ as an ASGI sub-app that BYPASSES the parent FastAPI CORSMiddleware. {"id":"python-factory-pfvo9","title":"EPIC: domain-agnostic reward signal — unpin recursive learning from security 'findings'","description":"PROBLEM: the recursive-learning reward signal is pinned to security "findings". The loop's only reward producer is games_process_workflow_rl -> evals_score_gt (findings vs gt_entries.json) -> reward = F1*100, gated by is_rl_eligible (findings-producing skills or graph_* tools). This is a domain leak (de-facto `if domain == security`) into the ENGINE, violating North Star #2 (domain = data, not branch). Non-finding work — ordinary chat, any non-security domain agent — can never be scored, rewarded, or learned from. Only spawned `swarm.completed`/`graph.completed` runs feed the loop; the main chat turn earns nothing.

GOAL: make reward a domain-agnostic POLYMORPHIC source. A reward signal = {scalar, verdict, provenance}. GT-findings becomes ONE adapter among several emitting the SAME neutral reward.computed contract (already domain-neutral: RewardComputedPayload has score/reward_value/verdict).

FRAMEWORK-FIRST (reuse what exists; no new ML, no bespoke RL):
- User feedback: chat-feedback.ts (bd-2dq6) already captures thumbs up/down to memory but dead-ends — wire it as an explicit reward source.
- LLM-as-judge: evals_evaluate / evals_evaluate_multi already exist (rubric-based, domain-agnostic, unused by the loop).
- Oracle verdict: the domain-agnostic oracle brick verdict (suspected->proven) as reward.
- Telemetry: tool failures/retries/errors from the events bus as negative reward/penalty.
- Findings/GT: demote to one adapter.
- Also: score the MAIN chat turn, not only spawned runs.

UNBLOCKS the offline trajectory landing-zone (every domain now yields scored trajectories).

DESIGN GATE (required before code): meta-architect (reward-source seam + neutral contract + zero domain branch) + strands-expert (how reward/recall attach to the live chat agent via Strands hooks/plugins). {"description":"Rando's synthesis (SDV/TimeGAN), training (LightGBM/LSTM/TCN), and eval (6 computational evaluators) pipelines are real and working, but three gaps were found via code audit + field-practice research (see .github/spec/can-failure-prediction-review.md):

1. All failure labels are hand-coded/synthetic, never validated against real faults. Current AUROC 0.97-1.00 numbers measure "detects the injected pattern" not "predicts vehicle failure."
2. No closed feedback loop exists despite the spec's stated "closed-loop adversarial system" goal. TimeGAN trains adversarially but only on unlabeled normal signals (never on failure modes), and is not called by the production can_run_full_pipeline / can_keystone.py.
3. The evals brick's 6 CAN computational evaluators are never called by can_keystone.py's training loop; LightGBM logs its own inline metrics instead.

This epic tracks the concrete child issues to close each gap.
"}

{"description":"Gap: every failure label in Rando is a hand-coded deterministic mutation (failure_injection.py, 8 modes: signal_drift, drop_to_zero, out_of_sequence, sensor_degradation, ecu_timeout, signal_freeze, spike_noise, correlation_break). No real fault timestamps exist anywhere in the pipeline. Current LightGBM AUROC 0.97-1.00 per CAN ID measures "can the model detect our own injected mutation," which is a materially easier task than "can it predict a real vehicle failure" — some CAN IDs hitting AUROC 1.000 with F1 flagged 0/1 is a signature of a too-easy synthetic task, not evidence of real predictive power.

Field context: synthetic failure injection ("the anomaly assumption") is a real, named weak-supervision technique, but the generalization gap between injected and real failure signatures is an explicitly documented open problem in the literature.

Fix, in priority order:
1. Source or construct a small set of REAL labeled fault episodes (even a labeled subset of a public dataset like Car-Hacking/OTIDS, or any DTC-linked real episode) and validate current LightGBM/LSTM/TCN performance against them. This is the single highest-value experiment — determines whether the construct-validity concern is theoretical or actually biting.
2. Lean into multi-signal correlated injection (correlation_break is the closest existing mode to how real faults usually manifest) over single-signal modes (drop_to_zero, freeze) as the primary training signal; treat single-signal modes as weaker positive controls.
3. In all reporting/dashboards, label current metrics explicitly as "detection of injected synthetic patterns," not "failure prediction accuracy," until step 1 is done.

Reference: .github/spec/can-failure-prediction-review.md section 4.
"}

{"description":"Gap: can_keystone.py's run_keystone_pipeline() (the function behind the can_run_full_pipeline MCP tool) hardcodes a fixed stage list — ingest, profile, synthesize (SDV only, via recipe://local/can-synthesize@1), window, augment, LightGBM — and never calls ml_train_timeseries(model_type="timegan") or ml_sample_timeseries anywhere. It's also only trained on unlabeled normal signal windows, not failure modes (y_uri is explicitly ignored for timegan per the MCP tool docstring), so even if wired in it would not currently generate model-driven failure examples (see the companion issue on hand-coded failure injection).

Additionally: current field trajectory (2024-2026 papers) shows diffusion models (TabDDPM, Diffusion-TS, CSDI) overtaking GANs as SOTA for time-series synthesis, and both GAN and diffusion families are documented as data-hungry — likely a poor fit for Rando's ~67 files / 48MB real-data corpus. TimeGAN maturation should be deprioritized relative to the label-validation gap (see companion issue), not invested in further right now.

Decision options (pick one explicitly, don't leave ambiguous):
1. [Recommended near-term] Leave TimeGAN as a documented, tested experiment; do not wire into can_keystone.py. Revisit only after real-label validation (companion issue) is done and if signal-fidelity (not label quality) turns out to be the actual bottleneck.
2. [If pursued] Build a conditional-GAN variant that takes a failure_mode label as generator input, so the adversarial loop can eventually target failure synthesis, not just normal-signal realism. This is the technically correct way to make "GAN vision" (generator improves, discriminator improves, both converge) actually apply to the failure side of the pipeline, which today it does not.
3. [If pursued] Evaluate a lightweight temporal VAE or revisit diffusion-based synthesis, but only once real fault data volume justifies a deep generative model.

Reference: .github/spec/can-failure-prediction-review.md sections 2 and 6.

{"description":"Gap: the spec (Rando.md, ml-dataset-generation.md) states the goal is a "closed-loop adversarial system... graded by evaluation metrics, until models achieve production-quality." No such loop exists in code. can_inference.py's CanInferenceBridge is a complete, working batch-inference class with ZERO connections to games, evals_persist_score, or memory_store anywhere in the codebase (confirmed by grep — it only appears in its own module, lazy-load registry, and MCP wrapper). Nothing feeds live inference errors, false alarms, or newly labeled episodes back into retraining.

Field context: production PHM systems favor drift-triggered retraining (PSI/KS/JS-divergence monitoring, e.g. Evidently AI/whylogs) over calendar-based retraining. Critically, a 2024 finding shows self-generated labels fed back into retraining WITHOUT a confirmation/filtering gate cause silent performance degradation over successive cycles.

Fix, in priority order (the plumbing already exists generically in events/games/memory per the platform's domain-agnostic substrate — this is wiring, not new infrastructure, except item 3):
1. Wire can_inference.py -> memory_store using the episode-tagging convention already specified in Rando.md section 10.5 (tags=["can-episode", ...]). This alone gets most of the way to a feedback loop.
2. Wire can_inference.py outputs into the events brick's learning contracts / rewards plumbing (same pattern games/workflow_rl.py already uses via get_service("tool_invoker")).
3. Design and implement a confirmation gate BEFORE wiring anything into games/RL retraining — decide what "confirmed" means for a real vehicle (DTC log match? human review?) so the system doesn't quietly reinforce its own synthetic-label biases. This is the one genuinely new component needed; do not skip it when wiring 1-2.
4. Add calibration-drift monitoring (not just static training-time Brier score) once live inference exists, plus a cost-sensitive/economic threshold instead of a fixed probability cutoff.

Reference: .github/spec/can-failure-prediction-review.md sections 5 and 7.

{"description":"Gap: the evals brick has 6 real, correctly-implemented, unit-tested CAN computational evaluators (can_auroc, can_auprc, can_brier, can_lead_time, can_false_alarm, can_episode_recall — plus 4 synthetic-data-fidelity evaluators: can_distribution_similarity, can_temporal_coherence, can_statistical_fidelity, can_mode_coverage) registered in evaluator_catalog.py. A bundler function evaluate_can_model() in evals/runtime/adapters/can_evaluator.py already wraps the classifier subset correctly. NONE of this is called by can_keystone.py's training loop — train_top_can_ids() (machine_learning/runtime/can_keystone_helpers.py) computes its own inline sklearn-style metrics via timeseries_metrics.py instead, duplicating logic that already exists correctly in evals.

Meta-architect verdict (already obtained): this is pure wiring debt, not a Polylith/dependency-direction violation. Two compounding gaps, both small:
(a) evaluate_can_model() has no MCP facade — only the lower-level evals_evaluate_computational(evaluator_name, ...) tool exists (scores one metric at a time on raw arrays). Nobody built the one-call convenience wrapper.
(b) machine_learning never calls evals at all — should push results to evals after training (not the other way around), using the exact same idiom the games brick's workflow_rl.py already uses: get_service("tool_invoker") from factory.mcp_utils.interface, then invoker("evals_evals_persist_score", ...) by bare tool-name string, no direct import of factory.evals.

Concrete fix (two additive changes, both small):
1. In evals/mcp/evaluator_tools.py, add a thin @mcp.tool() wrapper `evals_evaluate_can_model(y_true, y_pred, y_score)` that calls the existing evaluate_can_model() function. No new business logic — matches brick-anatomy.md.
2. In machine_learning/runtime/can_keystone_helpers.py::train_top_can_ids, after each trainer.train(...) call, look up the tool invoker and push validation predictions to the new evals tool, following workflow_rl.py's best-effort try/except pattern (log-and-swallow on failure, never raise).

Open design fork needing a decision before implementation: TimeSeriesTrainingJob.metrics is currently a flat dict[str,float] with no raw y_val/y_pred/y_score arrays to forward. Options: (a) widen the training job record to stash validation-split arrays at fit time [cheaper at runtime, touches a shared Pydantic contract], or (b) call trainer.predict(job.id, X_val_uri) after training to regenerate y_pred/y_score via the existing TimeSeriesTrainingPort.predict contract [architecturally cleaner, costs a redundant inference pass]. Route this specific fork through meta-architect + implementer before coding, since it spans two bricks and a shared contract shape.

Reference: .github/spec/can-failure-prediction-review.md section 5; meta-architect consult transcript in session history.
"}

{"id":"python-factory-sbhyq.1","title":"Validate CAN failure labels against real fault data (synthetic-injection construct-validity gap)","description":"Gap: every failure label in Rando is a hand-coded deterministic mutation (failure_injection.py, 8 modes: signal_drift, drop_to_zero, out_of_sequence, sensor_degradation, ecu_timeout, signal_freeze, spike_noise, correlation_break). No real fault timestamps exist anywhere in the pipeline. Current LightGBM AUROC 0.97-1.00 per CAN ID measures "can the model detect our own injected mutation," which is a materially easier task than "can it predict a real vehicle failure" — some CAN IDs hitting AUROC 1.000 with F1 flagged 0/1 is a signature of a too-easy synthetic task, not evidence of real predictive power.

Field context: synthetic failure injection ("the anomaly assumption") is a real, named weak-supervision technique, but the generalization gap between injected and real failure signatures is an explicitly documented open problem in the literature.

Fix, in priority order:
1. Source or construct a small set of REAL labeled fault episodes (even a labeled subset of a public dataset like Car-Hacking/OTIDS, or any DTC-linked real episode) and validate current LightGBM/LSTM/TCN performance against them. This is the single highest-value experiment — determines whether the construct-validity concern is theoretical or actually biting.
2. Lean into multi-signal correlated injection (correlation_break is the closest existing mode to how real faults usually manifest) over single-signal modes (drop_to_zero, freeze) as the primary training signal; treat single-signal modes as weaker positive controls.
3. In all reporting/dashboards, label current metrics explicitly as "detection of injected synthetic patterns," not "failure prediction accuracy," until step 1 is done.

Reference: .github/spec/can-failure-prediction-review.md section 4.

{"description":"Kiro session (2026-07-23) recommendation. See addendum in
`.github/spec/can-failure-prediction-review.md` and the Session Resume
entry in `.agents/steering/can-failure-prediction.md` (2026-07-23) for
full context and the field-research basis for this recommendation.

## Problem

Current `failure_injection.py`
(`components/dataset/src/factory/dataset/runtime/adapters/failure_injection.py`)
has 8 modes but most mutate a single signal in isolation (drop_to_zero,
signal_freeze, spike_noise, signal_drift, sensor_degradation). Real
faults usually manifest as a coordinated shift across multiple
correlated signals (e.g. coolant_temp rising + fan_rpm rising +
engine_load rising together), not one signal going to zero. This is
the leading theory (per `can-failure-prediction-review.md` and current
weak-supervision literature) for why AUROC 0.97-1.00 is inflated: the
model is likely learning to detect the injection method, not a real
failure signature. `correlation_break` is the closest existing mode to
"realistic" but only swaps two signals' values rather than modeling a
coordinated, physically-plausible shift.

This is decoupled from and does NOT need to wait on the real-label
validation work in `sbhyq.1` (which is blocked on external data
access) -- it is a pure engineering improvement to the existing
rule-based injector and can proceed now, independently.

## Work

1. Use the correlation matrix already computed by `can_profile.py` to
   identify signal clusters that move together.
2. Add a new failure mode (or extend `correlation_break`) that shifts
   a whole correlated cluster together in a physically consistent
   direction/magnitude, rather than single-signal drift/zero/freeze.
3. Constrain injected trajectories to the rate-of-change / delta
   thresholds `can_profile.py` already computes, so drift/spikes never
   exceed physically plausible slew rates for that signal.
4. Replace hard on/off failure-window label flips with a ramped
   onset/decay (gradual severity increase then decrease) instead of an
   instant `is_failure=1` window.
5. Reweight `failure_modes` defaults so multi-signal/correlated modes
   are the primary training signal and single-signal modes
   (drop_to_zero, signal_freeze, spike_noise) are documented as weaker
   positive controls, not primary signal -- this is a config/default
   change, not new injection code, per
   `can-failure-prediction-review.md` section 9.1 step 3.

## Acceptance

- New/extended correlated injection mode covers >=2 correlated signals
  per event, magnitude/direction consistent with the correlation sign.
- Injected deltas never exceed `can_profile`'s measured max
  rate-of-change for that signal (physical plausibility check,
  testable).
- Failure severity ramps in/out over the event window rather than an
  instant flip.
- `can_synthesize` default `failure_modes` weighting documented and
  updated to favor correlated modes.
- Existing failure_injection tests (`test_can_failure_modes.py`,
  `test_can_synthesize.py`) updated/extended, still green.
"}

{"description":"Kiro session (2026-07-23). `TimeGANAdapter`
(`components/machine_learning/src/factory/machine_learning/runtime/adapters/timegan.py`)
is unsupervised: it trains G/D on unlabeled NORMAL signal windows
only, `y_uri` is ignored. It structurally cannot generate failures no
matter how much it's tuned -- there is no failure-mode-conditioned
generator anywhere in the codebase. The 2026-07-21 GAN-loop
experiments (`.github/spec/can-gan-loop-report.md`) show unstable
AUROC across seeds (0.43-0.86), consistent with a GAN that is both
solving the wrong problem and data-starved on ~48MB of real captures.

Current published research (2025-2026) on few-shot fault time-series
generation has moved to diffusion models conditioned on normal-data
pretraining for exactly this low-data regime -- see FaultDiffusion
(arXiv 2511.15174) and Diff-MTS (arXiv 2407.11501), both reporting
diffusion beating GAN baselines on fault synthesis with scarce fault
data.

Do not keep iterating on the current unsupervised TimeGAN loop
expecting it to produce better failures -- it cannot, by construction.
Pick one explicitly:

1. [Recommended near-term, cheapest] Park TimeGAN as documented/tested
   code, invest instead in rule-based correlated injection (see
   companion bead `python-factory-bzm3s`) and real-label validation
   (`sbhyq.1`). Revisit generative modeling only if rule-based
   injection provably still looks "too fake."
2. Build a failure-mode-conditioned generator (conditional GAN or
   few-shot diffusion per the papers above) that takes a
   `failure_mode` label as input, so generator/discriminator
   convergence actually targets failure realism. This is new work, not
   a wiring fix.
3. Do nothing further with GAN loop iterations -- stop burning cycles
   on iteration 9-10 of the current demo-chart plan in the steering
   doc's "Session Resume" section, since the underlying metric
   instability is structural, not a seed-tuning problem.
"}

{"description":"GROUND TRUTH (verified at HEAD, commit 018a8f10, 2026-07-28):

1. Handover doc's claimed root cause is WRONG: _AVG_WINDOW=35 does not
   exist anywhere in git history (checked all commits + all local/remote
   branches). The actual constant is `_AVG_WINDOW = 4` in
   components/dataset/src/factory/dataset/runtime/adapters/failure_injection.py:66,
   unchanged since it was introduced in 58ae5738 (2026-07-15).

2. REAL bug #1 (dead code): `n_events = max(1, target_marked // _AVG_WINDOW)`
   followed by `if target_marked > 0 and n_events == 0: n_events = 1` --
   the second branch is unreachable dead code because max(1, ...) already
   guarantees n_events >= 1 even when target_marked == 0 (i.e. failure_rate
   configured but rounds to 0 events wanted). This forces at least ONE
   3-5-record failure window on every group, no matter how large.

3. REAL bug #2 (structural amplification): can_synthesize dispatches
   inject_failures() PER ARBITRATION ID (see _can_synthesize_dispatch.py),
   not once over the full record stream. Real CAN logs have dozens of
   arbitration IDs, many with small per-ID record counts after multiplier
   expansion (e.g. n_synth=4-20). For small n_synth, floor-division rate
   control (n_events = target_marked // 4) collapses to 1 forced event,
   and 1 event over a 4-20 record group is a 5-100% per-group rate. The
   overall corpus-level rate is the mean of these per-group rates, which
   skews high whenever many CAN IDs have small groups -- reproduced
   ACTUAL_RATE=0.91 vs configured 0.10 with a 100-ID / 1-frame-per-ID /
   multiplier=4 synthetic repro (see below). This structural mismatch
   between "rate control unit = per CAN ID" and "target rate = corpus-wide"
   is the real explanation for the ~89% observed in the handover doc,
   not a miscalibrated window constant.

4. TEST COVERAGE GAP CONFIRMED: none of the 4 commits since the handover
   doc (d49b80c0 correlation, 6d314ecc hybrid, 931cddfe scania extractor,
   0e7e3245 timegan conditional) added a test that asserts actual-vs-
   configured failure rate at the corpus/pipeline level. Ran all 4 test
   files: 83 passed, 2 skipped (external SCANIA fixture, unrelated).
   Every passing assertion is structural ("some failures exist", "labels
   use documented vocabulary", "mode X mutates the right field") -- none
   would fail under the 91% bug.
   - test_correlation_injection.py: only checks failures exist + correct
     mode label, never bounds the rate.
   - test_failure_injection_hybrid.py: bounds the RULE-VS-LEARNED MIX
     ratio (30/70 split, 0.10-0.55 tolerance) but never the overall
     is_failure rate vs failure_rate config.
   - test_scania_pattern_extractor.py / test_timegan_conditional.py:
     don't touch inject_failures/rate control at all (pattern extraction
     and conditional generation, orthogonal path).
   - The ONLY test with rate-adjacent bounds is
     test_can_synthesize.py::test_failure_rate_controls_fraction_of_failures,
     which asserts `fail_high <= 0.8 * len(high)` for failure_rate=0.30 --
     i.e. it explicitly TOLERATES up to 80% observed rate for a 30%
     target, so it would NOT catch the 89%-for-10%-target bug even if it
     ran. It's SKIPPED anyway (requires MF4 fixture at hardcoded
     /Users/danielrodrigo/Downloads/CAN Data, absent on this machine).
   - test_can_e2e_qa.py has `assert failure_rate_actual <= 0.5` for a
     0.1 target -- also too loose, and also skipped (same missing
     fixture).
   - The only automatic detector in production code is
     verify_failure_rate() in _post_injection_verification.py, which
     only logs a WARNING (never raises, never returns a signal) when
     |actual - expected| > 0.05. No test asserts on this log output
     (no caplog usage found for this module) -- confirmed via grep.

5. MINIMUM TEST THAT WOULD CATCH IT: a corpus-level (not single-group)
   property test that (a) calls the can_synthesize dispatch path (or
   inject_failures directly) across MULTIPLE small groups simulating
   realistic per-CAN-ID record counts, (b) computes actual_rate =
   total_failures / total_records across ALL groups combined, and
   (c) asserts abs(actual_rate - configured_rate) <= some tight tolerance
   (e.g. 0.03-0.05), for both single-group and multi-group/many-small-
   groups scenarios. None of the existing tests operate at this
   multi-group corpus level; they all check a single inject_failures()
   call on one homogeneous record list, which hides the amplification
   effect of many small per-ID groups.

Also found (separate, pre-existing) test breakage unrelated to the rate
bug: test_can_failure_modes.py::test_ecu_timeout_zeros_signals and
::test_signal_freeze_holds_constant FAIL at HEAD because
_physical_failure_modes.py (landed in 018a8f10, replacing the legacy

exact constant values the way the old _RULE_DISPATCH did -- the tests
were written against the pre-physical-modes semantics and never updated.
Filed as evidence of drift but out of scope for the rate bug itself."}

Design questions for the architecture gate, NOT to be decided unilaterally by the implementer:
1. What is the wire shape of an action? Prefer a typed reference to an MCP tool plus argument bindings over a free-form string. It must be impossible for a view payload to name an arbitrary HTTP endpoint.

4. Optimistic vs. authoritative refresh - does the action response carry a new view payload, or does the client re-fetch?
5. Idempotency for operational tools that spawn jobs, so a double-click cannot start two training runs.

Explicit non-goal: do not add a bespoke RPC layer. Everything routes through the existing MCP surface, because that is what keeps the human path and the agent path identical.

Lesson to carry from the dataset//ml//evals audit (epic python-factory-wvkvg): do not validate this against a mock of the tool layer. Test it against a real brick tool call. Two of the worst findings in that audit were adapters that passed tests because the test mocked the thing being integrated.

{"description":"Pre-existing bug (predates and is unrelated to the McpError->MCPError rename in GH issue #746). CatalogTool (components/mcp_utils/src/factory/mcp_utils/runtime/catalog_models.py) is a plain frozen dataclass with only name/description/fn -- it has NO .run() method. The real invocation path is ToolCatalog.call_tool(name, arguments) (async), which wraps invoke_native_tool and returns a native CallToolResult.

Dozens of test files across many bricks still call tool.run(arguments) or tool.run({...}) expecting the old FastMCP-era Tool.run() API (e.g. components/oracle/test/factory/oracle/test_mcp_contract.py, components/http_client/test/factory/http_client/test_mcp_contract.py, components/logger/test/factory/logger/test_mcp_contract.py, components/notification/test/factory/notification/test_typed_mcp_boundary.py, components/machine_learning/test/factory/machine_learning/test_can_model_config_preflight.py, components/machine_learning/test/factory/machine_learning/test_can_evaluation_persistence_roundtrip.py, components/machine_learning/test/factory/machine_learning/test_timeseries_model_config_mcp.py, components/evals/test/factory/evals/test_selected_typed_mcp.py, components/evals/test/factory/evals/test_ui_explorer_typed_mcp.py, components/payments/test/factory/payments/test_mcp_contract.py -- there are more, this is not exhaustive).

Confirmed via git stash that these failures exist identically on unmodified main -- this is not something my McpError-rename edits introduced.

Fix options:
1. Add a .run(arguments) compatibility shim to CatalogTool that delegates to the owning ToolCatalog.call_tool (requires CatalogTool to know its catalog, or a free helper function).
2. Update every failing test call site from tool.run(arguments) to catalog.call_tool(name, arguments) (matches the pattern already used correctly by components/agent, components/dataset, components/workflow, components/permissions tests).
Option 2 matches the already-correct pattern used elsewhere and avoids adding surface area to the immutable CatalogTool dataclass. Needs a sweep across all affected bricks; scope it as a discovered task with sub-tasks per brick if large."}

{"id":"python-factory-g8uf1","title":"Adapter-dispatch factories leak generic tool_execution_failed on unknown backend; no Protocol conformance check at registration","description":"Repo-wide gap in the Polymorphic/Agnostic adapter pattern (runtime/ports.py Protocol + runtime/runtime.py string-keyed dispatch), NOT a violation of the MCP-First tenet -- confirmed against .agents/steering/dev-principles.md: MCP-First governs cross-brick/agent-to-brick calls only, runtime/ internal adapter selection via plain Python is the documented, correct pattern. This bead is about hardening THAT pattern's failure mode, which is currently undocumented/unspecified.

Confirmed instances of the same shape: EvalsRuntime.get_runner (components/evals/src/factory/evals/runtime/runtime.py), TrackingRuntime._create_tracker/get_finetuner/get_timeseries_trainer (components/machine_learning/src/factory/machine_learning/runtime/runtime.py), GraphRuntime._create_graph (components/graph/src/factory/graph/runtime/runtime.py), GamesRuntime (components/games/src/factory/games/runtime/runtime.py), WorkerRuntime (bases/worker/src/factory/worker/runtime/runtime.py), APIRuntime (bases/api/src/factory/api/runtime/runtime.py).

Problem 1 -- lost diagnostic on unknown backend: every one of these factories raises a bare ValueError(f"Unknown {kind} backend: {backend}. Available: {self.available_backends()}") on an unrecognized backend string. The blanket exception-to-ToolResult wrapper in components/mcp_utils/src/factory/mcp_utils/runtime/typed_boundary.py (apply_category, ~line 131-189) catches this before it crosses the MCP wire (so the typed-egress guarantee holds -- no raw exception leaks), but it replaces the specific, actionable message with the generic tool_execution_failed sentinel, indistinguishable from any other internal bug. available_backends() already exists on every one of these runtimes for self-description (used in describe_config_schema/get_capabilities tools) but is never consulted defensively before dispatch to produce a typed domain-negative result (e.g. error=unknown_backend plus available_backends data).

Problem 2 -- no Protocol conformance check at registration: nothing in any of these factories isinstance-checks a concrete adapter against its runtime/ports.py Protocol at construction/registration time. Where @runtime_checkable is used (e.g. learning/runtime/ports.py::RewardSourcePort) it only verifies method NAMES exist, not signatures or completeness. A partially-implemented adapter can be registered and only fail the first time something calls the specific missing method, discovered at call time as an AttributeError swallowed by the same generic tool_execution_failed sentinel.

Discovered while investigating GH issue #746 (FastMCP removal) and a follow-up conversation about whether the RL learning loop's evals_score_gt/evals_evaluate_multi calls were at risk from adapter swaps -- they are NOT (those two tools bypass get_runner entirely, confirmed by direct code read), but the investigation surfaced this real, separate, repo-wide gap in the adapter-dispatch pattern itself.","acceptance_criteria":"Design and land a typed domain-negative result for unknown-backend selection (e.g. a shared helper each get_runner/get_tracker/get_graph/etc factory calls, returning a typed unknown_backend failure with available_backends data instead of raising bare ValueError) across at minimum evals, machine_learning, graph, games, worker, api runtimes. Add a registration-time Protocol conformance check (structural isinstance against runtime_checkable Protocol at minimum; consider signature-level checks) so an incomplete adapter fails fast at wiring time rather than at first missing-method call. Document the resulting pattern in .agents/steering/brick-anatomy.md's adapter section so future bricks follow it by default.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"wdaniero@amazon.com","created_at":"2026-08-28T12:16:12Z","created_by":"Daniel Rodrigo","updated_at":"2026-08-28T12:16:12Z"}

1. POST /api/tools/{tool_name} invokes ANY aggregator tool from an unauthenticated JSON body. Verified:
     curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/tools/cache_health_check -d '{}'  ->  HTTP 200 with real result
   bases/api/runtime/bridge.py::execute_tool calls _extract_envelope, which returns None when there is no Bearer token, and then proceeds to _call_tool anyway.

2. /api/health reports total_tools: 689. All of them are reachable this way, including @authoring tools (persona create/delete, config mutation) and cost-bearing operational ones (agent_agent_launch_swarm, sandbox Docker provisioning, ledger writes).

On any shared network the whole tool surface is reachable by anyone who can route to the host. scripts/companion-x-ui.sh sets no host override, so the normal local dev path is the exposed path.
